text:
incident-bot: PAGER — svc-proxy auth anomaly detected. sudden 10x spike in auth attempts to /v1/ingest from multiple clients, 401->200 transition for token:svc-*. rate: ~8200 requests/min, suspicious user-agents. flagged by anomaly-detector at 2026-03-15T02:00:34Z. link: https://internal/alerts/2750001234

sara_oncall: acked. I'm on call, pulling logs now. tagging @mike_sre and @julia_prodsec.

mike_sre: looking at proxy logs — huge batch of retries from a small set of source IPs (10 distinct /24s). But interestingly a subset of requests show valid service-account tokens (svc-account-prod-1) beginning ~02:00:20Z. request-id sample: aa3f... status sequence: 401,401,200.

julia_prodsec: that pattern = credential scraping + replay. Could be leaked token or credential stuffing at scale. We should assume compromise of svc-account-prod-1 until proven otherwise.

sara_oncall: containment plan: 1) block offending CIDRs at edge WAF + load balancer 2) disable svc-account-prod-1 3) rotate keys and issue new creds behind a canary 4) throttle all non-internal traffic to /v1/ingest.

ashley_support: if we disable svc-account-prod-1, which customers are impacted? I have the mapping, will DM a list and prepare customer comms for tenants using that SA.

mike_sre: getting live pcap from egress VPC and dumping recent KV cache hits for tokens. quick grep shows token last used from 3 distinct regions: eu-west-1, us-east-1, ap-southeast-1. suspicious but aligns with replay.

ops-bot: action started: WAF rule 4101 applied (block cidrs: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 192.0.2.0/24).

sara_oncall: WAF blocks in place. starting service account disable now. Mike, temp remove read access to ingestion buckets and revoke long-lived session tokens for svc-account-prod-1.

mike_sre: running rotation sequence. snippet below used to rotate via key-service API (internal):

```
# rotate service account key (internal control plane)
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/service-accounts/svc-account-prod-1/rotate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"rotate_kms":true, "invalidate_sessions": true}'
# followup: wait for new key to become active, then update consumers
```

julia_prodsec: after rotation, we need to do post-rotate monitoring and an output-quality check for any downstream inference jobs that may break. schedule canary with 1% traffic first. also open SOC ticket and capture full raw logs for legal.

ashley_support: prod customer list (prelim): customer-42, analytic-ops, partner-eval. Preparing status banner/template. Will have copy in 10 mins.

sara_oncall: rotation command returned success at 02:03:02Z. invalidation flag set. now revoking active sessions:

```
# revoke active sessions
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/sessions/revoke" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"service_account":"svc-account-prod-1","reason":"suspected compromise"}'
```

mike_sre: sessions revoke completed. I can still see retries from blocked CIDRs but 401->200 pattern stopped for that token. good signal.

julia_prodsec: recommend full key rotation for any tokens that were created in the last 72h for that SA and search S3 audit trails for uploads matching token id. escalate to legal if PII appears.

ashley_support: drafted customer notice: short ack, what we know, mitigation steps, ETA for followup. pinging @eng-customer-notify to review.

sara_oncall: next steps: 1) finish log capture and archive 2) run access scan for other SAs with similar token lifetimes 3) create post-incident runbook item for tighter token TTLs 4) schedule incident retro. Assigning tasks: mike -> logs+pcap capture + NAT egress block verification; julia -> SOC/legal + post-rotate validation; ashley -> customer comms; sara -> incident doc and severity classification.

ops-bot: create-ticket: INC-2026-275000 (priority P1) created and assigned. link: https://internal/incident/INC-2026-275000

mike_sre: captured pcap and uploaded to secure bucket s3://secure-incidents/INC-2026-275000/pcap.pcap. grep shows no obvious exfil beyond auth headers but will hand off to forensics.

julia_prodsec: forensics: collect memory snapshots for proxy pods that handled the requests, and check CI/CD pipeline for any recent credential exposures. Also check ACLs on logging pipeline — ensure logs with tokens were not forwarded externally.

sara_oncall: marking thread resolved for immediate customer impact: auth flow is contained, blocked IPs and rotated keys, tokens invalidated. Leaving incident open for forensics and comms.

ashley_support: posting initial customer banner now. will post update after legal signoff. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: RESOLVE_CHECK — automated followup scheduled in 6h to verify no recurrence.

sara_oncall: thanks team. handoff to daytime on-call @mike_sre in 2h for continued monitoring. closing live page.
